content:
If classic cinema holds a special place in your heart, it's time to make a little extra space in your movie library. The original King Kong, from 1933, is getting a 4K release as a steelbook and a collector's edition. It doesn't have an official release date just yet, but preorders for both are already available at several different retailers, which we've broken down below.

While the release date is still TBD, it's well worth preordering your preferred copy now before these shops run out of stock. Already the collector's edition has sold out at Gruv (which is an online retailer owned by Universal Pictures ), so they're going fast. If you're eager to have it on your shelves, now is the time to buy.

Preorder King Kong (1933) – Collector’s Edition

See at Amazon - $59.99

See at Walmart - $74.96

See at Gruv - $59.99 (SOLD OUT)

Both releases have classic black-and-white casing (though the images for them do say 'temporary art' in the corner, so that will likely change closer to release), featuring 'King Kong' across the front. Compared to the regular steelbook, the collector's edition comes with a few extra items alongside the film on 4K. These are: a movie ticket replica, a two-sided movie poster, and five lobby cards, plus a box to hold everything.

As of the time of this writing, there doesn't seem to be any mention of bonus features. However, if that changes we'll update this piece with what they are.

Preorder King Kong (1933) – Limited Edition Steelbook

See at Walmart - $29.96

See at Gruv - $32.99

See at Amazon - $34.99

The steelbook features the same design as above, though doesn't come with all of the extra goodies. If you're just looking to have the film on 4K UHD and digital, this can set you up with what you need.

We consider the original King Kong to be among the best monster movies of all time, so it's certainly worth adding to your physical media library if you adore the classics. And if you're looking for even more 4Ks and Blu-rays to add to your library right now, your timing couldn't be better.

Black Friday sales are officially live, and there are a ton of movie and TV show deals to look through. These are sure to stick around through Cyber Monday as well, so you have plenty of time to shop for your favorites while they're still discounted.
